cases.structural_justification: n_boot=200 parametric-bootstrap percentile CI endpoints carry substantial Monte Carlo error on each engine independently (R's bootstrap_Sigma()-based route and Julia's repeatability_bootstrap_ci() route are two SEPARATE stochastic simulate-refit procedures with no shared seed/replicate correspondence) -- a numeric endpoint-distance bar at any n_boot=200-scale tolerance is not a meaningful cross-engine check (wave5-conversion4 showed 0.52 vs the already-loose 0.05 bar). REPAIR (2026-09-01): re-typed as a structural check on EACH engine's own bootstrap CI independently -- finite endpoints, lower <= upper, and lower <= point_estimate <= upper (point estimate from that engine's own repeatability_point route) -- rather than a fabricated numeric pass. The numerically comparable ICC routes remain CI-ROUTE-008 (default->wald) and CI-ROUTE-010 (explicit wald), both still endpoint-tolerance cases at 1e-3.

cases.layout_note: R's extract_cutpoints()$tau_estimate reports only the K-2 FREE cutpoints per trait (Hadfield 2015 convention: tau_1 = 0 fixed for identifiability, never reported). GLLVM.jl's OrdinalPerTraitFit.tau is a p x (C-1) matrix whose FIRST column is the fixed tau_1 = 0.0 (src/families/ordinal.jl: `tau[t, 1] = 0.0`). REPAIR (2026-09-01, wave5-conversion4: r_len=5 vs julia_len=10, i.e. R's p free cutpoints vs Julia's p*(C-1) INCLUDING the fixed column): the Julia side now flattens tau[:, 2:end] (dropping the fixed tau_1 column) to match R's free-cutpoints-only convention exactly. With C=3 (ordinal_small), that is 1 free cutpoint per trait, p=5 traits -> 5 entries on both sides.

Julia surface exists (extract_communality(fit::GllvmFit) = communality(fit), src/confint_derived.jl), but the two engines compute a DIFFERENT ESTIMAND, not just a different call shape -- traced both to source. GLLVM.jl's communality(fit) denominator is sigma_y_site(fit), the FULL model-implied total variance across ALL tiers PLUS sigma_eps^2 (the Gaussian observation residual). R's extract_communality(fit, level) denominator is extract_Sigma(fit, level, part='total')$Sigma -- a SINGLE TIER's total only; sigma_eps^2 never enters any R extract_communality/extract_Sigma tier computation for a Gaussian fit at all (it is not one of the 'B'/'W'/'phy' component tiers the R tier system tracks). On gaussian_small (unique=FALSE, no W tier): level='unit' degenerates to an uninformative constant 1.0 for every trait (shared_B == total_B exactly, since there is no diag_B term to make them differ) -- confirmed the observed wave5-conversion4 diff (0.871) is exactly this: R's degenerate ~1.0 vs Julia's real shared/(shared+sigma_eps^2) ratio. level='unit_obs' returns NULL outright (fit$use$rr_W is FALSE, no W-tier loadings). No R call on this fixture targets the same 'shared vs grand total including the Gaussian residual' estimand Julia computes; this is a genuine cross-engine definition mismatch, not a fixable call bug. REPAIR (2026-09-01, wave5-conversion4): moved from cases[] to deferred[].

Julia surface exists (extract_correlations(fit::GllvmFit) = correlation(fit), src/confint_derived.jl), but traced both definitions to source (same class of mismatch as extract_communality). GLLVM.jl's correlation(fit) standardises by sigma_y_site(fit), the FULL model-implied total variance INCLUDING sigma_eps^2. R's route for this quantity (extract_Sigma(fit, level='unit', part='total')$R -- used because extract_correlations() itself returns an un-coercible long-format table, not a matrix) standardises by the 'unit' (B) tier total only, which never includes sigma_eps^2 for a Gaussian fit. On gaussian_small this produces a materially different correlation matrix (observed max_abs_diff 0.668, wave5-conversion5) -- a genuine cross-engine estimand mismatch, not a fixable call bug. REPAIR (2026-09-01): moved from cases[] to deferred[], joining extract_communality in the maintainer's estimand-alignment decision.

Julia surface exists (extract_proportions(fit::GllvmFit; component) forwards to proportions(fit; component), src/confint_derived.jl), but traced to source: this is the SAME estimand mismatch as extract_communality, exactly -- extract_proportions(fit; component=:shared) IS communality(fit) mathematically (both ΛΛ^T[t,t] / sigma_y_site(fit)[t,t], the FULL total-variance denominator incl. sigma_eps^2). R's extract_proportions()'s 'shared_unit' component's proportion column denominator (total <- rowSums(M)) only ever sums the tier-scoped components R's system tracks; sigma_eps^2 is not one of them, so on gaussian_small (only the shared_unit component present) proportion degenerates to shared_unit/shared_unit == 1.0 for every trait -- the exact reason the observed max_abs_diff (0.8713, wave5-conversion5) matched extract_communality's own failure value precisely. REPAIR (2026-09-01): moved from cases[] to deferred[], joining extract_communality and extract_correlations in the maintainer's estimand-alignment decision.

Julia surface exists (extract_Omega(fit::GllvmFit), src/extractors.jl), but traced both compositions to source (wave5-conversion6). R's extract_Omega() sums ONLY the covariance tiers the fit actually carries -- gaussian_small has no W-tier (fit$use$rr_W and diag_W both FALSE), so R's tiers = 'B' only and Omega = Lambda_B Lambda_B^T exactly, with sigma_eps^2 never entering (it is not one of the B/W/phy component tiers R's tier system tracks; the Gaussian family's link_residual_per_trait() contributes 0 separately). GLLVM.jl's extract_Omega(fit::GllvmFit) UNCONDITIONALLY sums extract_Sigma(level=:unit,...).Sigma .+ extract_Sigma(level=:unit_obs,...).Sigma, and extract_Sigma(level=:unit_obs, part=:total) ALWAYS adds sigma_eps^2*I as a baseline term regardless of whether a genuine W-tier exists (src/extractors.jl's _sigma_unit_obs). So on gaussian_small, Julia's Omega = Lambda_B Lambda_B^T + sigma_eps^2*I, differing from R's by exactly sigma_eps^2 on the diagonal -- confirmed: the observed max_abs_diff (0.467) is diagonal-scale and close to sigma_true^2=0.49, matching this trace exactly. extract_Omega(fit::GllvmFit) takes NO tiers/level/link_residual kwargs at all (unlike getResidualCov's alignable level= argument), so there is no call-argument fix available. Also tried sourcing the R comparand as extract_Sigma(level='unit_obs',...)$Sigma directly (mirroring the extract_correlations substitution): R's own tier-existence gate returns NULL for level='unit_obs' on this single-tier fixture (the same gate behind wave5-conversion4's residual_cov r_len=0), so R's tier system has no way to express the Gaussian residual variance independent of a genuine W-tier at all -- the same structural gap already deferred for extract_communality/extract_correlations/extract_proportions. REPAIR (2026-09-01): moved from cases[] to deferred[], joining the estimand-alignment family (4th member: communality, correlations, proportions, Omega).
